request: Check whether the project can be put on a pilot server and used by real developers (install CLI, connect MCP, develop, deploy), and review the boundary between core/platform and user code.
source: Working tree: uncommitted 0.10.0 candidate plus the 2026-11-15 review fixes. The public server runs 0.9.0 from 173c6d5 and was only read.

checks.command: curl of /api/health on the portal, dev portal and console; /api/v1/capabilities; /api/v1/cli/install; /mcp and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource; systemctl is-active miy-v2-serve miy-v2-worker
checks.observed: Three health endpoints 200; serverVersion 0.9.0; cliVersion 0.9.0 from 173c6d5 with 5 downloads, 2 tunnel images and the Windows installer; /mcp answers 401 with protected-resource metadata naming the console issuer; both services active.

checks.name: Published CLI downloads
checks.observed: 7 downloads, 250,963,545 bytes, version 0.9.0, commit and hashes match.

checks.name: Disposable full stack: server assembly, Keycloak login, CLI build and deploy, app frame
checks.scope: bootstrap of an empty state directory, platform and frame-runtime builds, PostgreSQL/Keycloak/Caddy, migrate, seed, serve and worker; then with the working-tree CLI: login, component publish, app init, component sync, register, approve, commit, app build, app deploy (two releases), status; then in a browser: Keycloak login, the deployed app in its frame on the dev portal, health, stop/start, unsaved-input guard, release change, frame isolation from portal/console/IdP, permission revocation while open, removal.
checks.limits: HTTP on localhost with a port pool for frames; CLI login through the fixture development accounts, not a device approval; local Docker build, not --remote; no app dev preview, no MCP client, no prod promotion.

checks.scope: offline: command discovery and manuals, MCP default/command/search discovery against the installed CLI, setup repeatability, project MCP configuration, explicit 0.9.0 to 0.10.0 upgrade preserving business code, applied SQL, components and dependency versions
checks.note: The installed 0.9.0 server binary was only read as the baseline. The four executable copies this run left in its evidence directory were removed; result.json is kept.

checks.scope: disposable PostgreSQL; second run, after the fixture change below

checks.name: Server build persistence and API (app build --remote)
checks.scope: disposable PostgreSQL: request dedup, upload, permissions and revocation, queue limits, logs. No real Rust compile on a server worker is part of this check; second run, after the fixture change below

checks.name: PostgreSQL semantics of the build-time migration history read
checks.command: disposable postgres:18.3 container (--network none, tmpfs, removed afterwards): the role layout of worker.rs prepare_resource, a migration run as the app owner that renames _sqlx_migrations and replaces it with a view calling its own function, then the exact statements of verify_development_migrations as the postgres superuser
checks.observed: As the app owner the function reports is_superuser=off and cannot read pg_authid. In the platform's read-only repeatable-read transaction as the provisioning superuser the same function runs with current_user=postgres, is_superuser=on and reads pg_authid.
checks.limits: Only the read side was exercised. A complete hostile migration applied by sqlx and a real server build were not run.

openGaps.evidence: up.sh runs the root build (platform and fixtures only) and never builds @miy/frame-runtime into the state directory; stack-ui.sh does it by hand. Tracked as R12 in docs/PLAN.md order 6.

boundaryFindings.verified: code read and isolated PostgreSQL check
boundaryFindings.finding: A server build reads app._sqlx_migrations of the app's dev database as the provisioning superuser (crates/miy/src/worker.rs:417-434, called from server_build_worker.rs:408 and :540; PROVISION_DATABASE_URL is the postgres superuser in scripts/bootstrap.py:238). That relation is owned by the role that runs developer migrations (worker.rs:636), and migration SQL is checked only for transaction control. Developer-defined code can therefore run as database superuser, above the core, identity and every app database.

boundaryFindings.verified: code read; the failure scenarios were not run
boundaryFindings.finding: A locally built, uploaded image is checked for labels, platform, manifest, migrations, UI and commit only (crates/miy/src/runtime.rs:616-685). /miy is copied out with no size or file-type limit and regular files are read whole in the worker's sequential control lane (crates/miy/src/contract.rs:108-131). The protected SDK and components are verified only by app build --remote (crates/miy/src/source_archive.rs); the contract says the bundle lock is a reproducibility check, not a security boundary (templates/rust-react/docs/CONTRACT.md:19).
No egress restriction for app containers: each installation gets a bridge network with the shared PostgreSQL attached as 'postgres' and ordinary outbound access (crates/miy/src/runtime.rs:966-1005).

boundaryFindings.verified: reported by the server-side review; not re-read here
boundaryFindings.finding: Migrations run without a statement or lock timeout in the worker's sequential control loop, so one app's long migration delays every app's operations.

boundaryFindings.verified: code read for the items named
boundaryFindings.finding: The ownership boundary inside a generated project is enforced by three hash locks but described incompletely: the protected path lists are kept by hand in four places, recovery output and the UI 1.1.0 README name the removed command 'app components' (crates/miy/src/component_cli.rs:694, scripts/build-ui-component.mjs:41), and a remote build silently leaves out tracked files outside its allowlist (crates/miy/src/source_archive.rs:169-171).

boundaryReviewMethod: Two read-only code reviews (generated project/CLI/MCP, and server enforcement/isolation); the claims listed above were then checked against the code, and rank 1 against PostgreSQL.
